sections.html:
Sumter County lies in central South Carolina and spans roughly 682 square miles. The city of Sumter is the seat and the biggest community, with 43,463 residents at the 2020 count; the county as a whole had 105,556. The Wateree River runs along the western line, the Black River drains much of the land, and Lake Marion touches the southern part.

If your house sits close to the Wateree, the Black River or the lake, look at the flood maps before you put it on the market. Lenders check them.

Shaw Air Force Base is the best-known employer, and military households sometimes have to sell fast when orders change. Manufacturing is the largest job sector, at about 18 percent. Very old deeds can be tricky: land that once belonged to Clarendon County may have records filed under that county's name, so a title search is worth ordering for family land.

sections.h2: Who to call about your tax bill
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Treasurer work out of one building at 13 East Canal Street, Sumter, SC 29150. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The county's main number is 803-436-2102, and the delinquent tax line is 803-436-2213.

Phone numbers on county pages vary a little, so if one rings out, ask for the Treasurer by name of the office and keep whichever number connects.

Roughly, the Assessor sets the value and classification of your property, the Auditor handles exemptions, and the Treasurer collects the money. Bring your parcel number when you call, because every office will ask for it first.

Notices go out in October. You can pay through January 15 with no added charge. Pay online through the county's qpaybill system, by mail or in person.

If paid afterExtra charge on base tax
January 153%
February 110%
March 1615%

The online screens may leave off penalties and fees, so get the true payoff from the Treasurer before you send a payment or close a sale.

South Carolina law lets a county council allow installment payments by ordinance. Ask the Treasurer whether Sumter County has done so before you count on splitting a bill.

A house that is the owner's legal residence is assessed at 4 percent of value. Other residential property is assessed at 6 percent. Apply for the lower rate with the Assessor as soon as you move in, and report within 30 days if the home stops being your domicile. A home wrongly classed at 6 percent costs real money every year.

  • Increases from a reassessment are capped at 15 percent for tax purposes.
  • The Assessor mails a notice when fair market value rises by $1,000 or more.
  • Homestead exemption: owners who are 65 or older, totally disabled or legally blind, and who have lived in South Carolina for one year, exclude the first $50,000 of the legal residence's value. Apply at the County Auditor's Office.
  • Some disabled veterans and surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty may be exempt on the home and up to five acres, through the SC Department of Revenue.

Call the Assessor to learn when the next reassessment is scheduled.

Send a written appeal to the County Assessor within 90 days of the date on the assessment notice. You don't need to wait for the tax bill.

  1. If the matter is still open on December 31, you are billed on at least 80 percent of the current assessed value.
  2. You can ask in writing to be billed on more than 80 percent, which limits interest if you lose.
  3. The bill is still due January 15.
  4. When the appeal ends, you get a refund or pay the difference plus interest.

Appeals of Department of Revenue assessments run on a separate track with their own 90-day protest rule.

Unpaid real estate and mobile home taxes lead to the delinquent tax sale. This year the Treasurer's notice sets the sale for December 8, 2026, and taxes must be paid by 5 p.m. on December 7, 2026 to pull a property out of it. Phone the Treasurer at 803-436-2213 to confirm the date, because sale dates can move.

After a sale, South Carolina gives the owner 12 months to redeem. Interest rises with time: 3, 6, 9 or 12 percent depending on the quarter in which you redeem. The county must send a certified mail notice between 45 and 20 days before the redemption period ends.

Get the payoff in writing from the Treasurer, with penalties included, and find out how near any sale date is. Check that the home is classed as your legal residence at 4 percent and fix it if not. If a reappraisal notice came, compare the sale price with the new assessment, since a gap may be worth an appeal.

At closing, unpaid tax is subtracted from the seller's proceeds, so there are no loose ends for the buyer. A title company will ask for the figure early, which is why a quick call to the Treasurer pays off. If the house is inherited, make sure the person selling is the person who actually holds title.

We buy Sumter County houses as-is, including homes with back taxes and inherited property. Send us the address and tell us what is owed, and we will explain what a cash sale would look like.

sections.h2: What to bring when you visit the offices
sections.html:
Take the latest tax notice, the parcel or tax map number and a photo ID. For a homestead or legal residence claim, bring proof of age or disability if it applies and proof you live in the home. For an appeal, bring the assessment notice and whatever supports your number, such as recent sales of similar homes nearby. Written requests are safer than phone calls when a deadline is involved.

Keep copies of anything you hand in, and note the name of the clerk who helped you and the date.

faqs.q: When are Sumter County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By January 15 without penalty. After that the county adds 3 percent, then 10 percent after February 1 and 15 percent after March 16.

faqs.q: When is the Sumter County tax sale?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's notice sets it for December 8, 2026, with payment due by 5 p.m. on December 7 to avoid the sale. Confirm with the Treasurer at 803-436-2213.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Sumter County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date on the assessment notice. File in writing with the Assessor, and pay on time because an appeal doesn't delay the due date.

faqs.q: What is the legal residence rate in Sumter County?
faqs.a: An owner-occupied home that is the owner's legal residence is assessed at 4 percent, and other residential property at 6 percent. You apply through the Assessor.

faqs.q: Can I get the homestead exemption in Sumter County?
faqs.a: If you are 65 or older, totally disabled or legally blind and have lived in South Carolina for one year, you can exclude the first $50,000 of your home's value. Apply at the County Auditor's Office.
